payment_support@1.population: Accounts with at least one failed invoice payment before the snapshot, still inside the grace period at the snapshot, and contactable on a permitted channel.
eligibility_rules: contact_consent granted and not withdrawn at t0
no retention contact inside the cooldown window before t0

timing.time_zero_rule: Nightly snapshot at 02:00 local time on the day an account enters the failed-payment grace period; eligibility, assignment and follow-up all start there.

payment_support@1.endpoint: Administrative cancellation recorded in the subscription status ledger within the horizon, counted from t0.
payment_support@1.estimand: ITT: E[Y(dunning_only) - Y(a)] over the eligible cohort as assigned at t0, positive means cancellation prevented.
payment_support@1.inference_method: Cross-fitted doubly robust scores with paired policy contrasts; cluster-robust intervals at the randomization unit.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Final at t0 + 90 days + 30 days ingest lag, i.e. day 120; corrections accepted for a further 30 days.
endpoints.description: Administrative cancellation recorded in the subscription status ledger.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Same maturity as cancellation90; the effect inherits the slowest arm.
endpoints.description: ITT contrast on cancellation90, sign-flipped so that higher is better.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Invoice-level postings settle on a 45-day cycle; final at t0 + 135 days, after refunds and reversals.
endpoints.description: Retained margin net of posted action cost. ASSUMPTION: no partner ledger has confirmed these postings.

deployment_bounds: Decision support only; a human approves every contact list.
Scope is the failed-payment population, not the whole customer base.
No conclusion transfers to another operator, channel or offer version.
assumptions: ASSUMPTION: grace period is a fixed, reproducible field in the billing ledger.
ASSUMPTION: contact cost and offer cost are posted once each, to the account.
ASSUMPTION: no partner has confirmed that a payment-support contact is operationally available.
open_questions: Who owns the action and can stop it?
Can assignment, delivery and outcome be distinguished in the source systems?
Is there a cost ledger with actual postings rather than allocated overhead?

payment_support_delivered_only@1.population: Same frame as payment_support, restricted after randomization to accounts whose contact was actually delivered.
eligibility_rules: BROKEN ON PURPOSE: delivery_succeeded == true, evaluated after t0
payment_support_delivered_only@1.endpoint: Administrative cancellation recorded in the subscription status ledger within the horizon, counted from t0.
payment_support_delivered_only@1.estimand: NEGATIVE CONTROL: per-protocol-like contrast conditioned on post-assignment delivery; not an ITT effect.
payment_support_delivered_only@1.inference_method: Same estimator as the reference protocol, applied to a deliberately broken cohort.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Final at t0 + 90 days + 30 days ingest lag, i.e. day 120; corrections accepted for a further 30 days.
endpoints.description: Administrative cancellation recorded in the subscription status ledger.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Same maturity as cancellation90; the effect inherits the slowest arm.
endpoints.description: ITT contrast on cancellation90, sign-flipped so that higher is better.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Invoice-level postings settle on a 45-day cycle; final at t0 + 135 days, after refunds and reversals.
endpoints.description: Retained margin net of posted action cost. ASSUMPTION: no partner ledger has confirmed these postings.

assumptions: Selection on delivery is the bias being measured, not a modelling choice.

payment_support_survivor_cohort@1.population: Same frame as payment_support, restricted to accounts still active on the day the agent reached them.
eligibility_rules: BROKEN ON PURPOSE: still active at delivery_at, evaluated after t0
payment_support_survivor_cohort@1.endpoint: Administrative cancellation recorded in the subscription status ledger within the horizon, counted from t0.
payment_support_survivor_cohort@1.estimand: NEGATIVE CONTROL: contrast on a cohort that survived until contact; immortal time by construction.
payment_support_survivor_cohort@1.inference_method: Same estimator as the reference protocol, applied to a deliberately broken cohort.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Final at t0 + 90 days + 30 days ingest lag, i.e. day 120; corrections accepted for a further 30 days.
endpoints.description: Administrative cancellation recorded in the subscription status ledger.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Same maturity as cancellation90; the effect inherits the slowest arm.
endpoints.description: ITT contrast on cancellation90, sign-flipped so that higher is better.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Invoice-level postings settle on a 45-day cycle; final at t0 + 135 days, after refunds and reversals.
endpoints.description: Retained margin net of posted action cost. ASSUMPTION: no partner ledger has confirmed these postings.

assumptions: Immortal-time selection is the bias being measured.

hillstrom_mens_email@1.population: Customers who purchased in the twelve months before the campaign and were eligible to receive marketing e-mail.
eligibility_rules: purchased within the twelve months before t0
holds a deliverable e-mail address at t0

timing.time_zero_rule: The moment the campaign was sent; eligibility, assignment and follow-up all start there.

hillstrom_mens_email@1.endpoint: Conversion recorded within two weeks of the send, counted from t0.
hillstrom_mens_email@1.estimand: ITT: E[Y(mens_email) - Y(no_email)] over the eligible cohort as assigned at t0; positive means conversions gained.
hillstrom_mens_email@1.inference_method: Cross-fitted doubly robust scores with paired policy contrasts; studentized bootstrap intervals over the customer.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Final at t0 + 14 days; the source records no later corrections.
endpoints.description: Purchase recorded within two weeks of the send.
Site visit within two weeks. An intermediate step, not the decision endpoint.

endpoints.maturity_rule: Same window as conversion14; the source reports no refunds or reversals.
endpoints.description: Money spent within two weeks. Zero for the large majority of customers.

deployment_bounds: Method study on a public dataset; not a recommendation for any operator.
Two-week readout only; nothing here speaks to longer-horizon effects.
The third arm (womens_email) exists in the data and is not the primary contrast.
assumptions: ASSUMPTION: assignment was randomised as the source describes; this repository has not audited it.
ASSUMPTION: the three arms share one eligible frame, so the control arm is a valid comparator.
open_questions: Does an assignment audit on 8 covariates reject exchangeability the way it did for Orange?
Is spend the right reward, or is conversion the decision-relevant endpoint?
